mainTopic: נר חנוכה: lighting is the מצוה, who may light, oils, the ברכות and their basis, and lighting at two entrances because of חשד.
overview: The גמרא proves from a ברייתא about a lantern, and from the wording of the ברכה, that הדלקה עושה מצוה: the lighting is the מצוה. So a חרש, שוטה, or קטן cannot light, but a woman can, since women were also part of the miracle. רב ששת rules that an אכסנאי must take part in נר חנוכה, and רבי זירא tells how he did this. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that all oils are fine for the lamp and for ink, but שמן זית is best, and the גמרא briefly discusses how ink is made. Next come the ברכות: both the one who lights and the one who sees make a ברכה, and שהחיינו is said only on the first night. The גמרא explains that we can say 'וצונו' on a rabbinic מצוה because of 'לא תסור'. It then asks why דמאי gets no ברכה, and אביי and רבא answer in different ways. Finally, a חצר with entrances on two sides needs two lights because of חשד, and the גמרא begins to prove from the laws of פאה that the תורה cares about suspicion. That proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A lantern that burned all through שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: a lantern that burned all of שבת must be put out after שבת and lit again for חנוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A lantern that kept burning the whole day of שבת: after שבת ends, one puts it out and lights it again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to settle its open question: is the מצוה the lighting or the placing? This step only quotes the source. The next step explains how it proves anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lantern is already burning, and it is already in its place. The ברייתא still says you must put it out and relight it, so an existing flame does not count by itself.

phrases.english: A lantern that was continuing to burn
the entire day (of Shabbat),
at the end of Shabbat, one extinguishes it and lights it.
phrases.notes: It is relit so that it serves as the נר חנוכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשָׁשִׁית שֶׁהָיְתָה דּוֹלֶקֶת וְהוֹלֶכֶת כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier attempts (on the previous amud) to decide between הדלקה עושה מצוה and הנחה עושה מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a lantern burning through שבת

steps.title: Why the lantern case shows lighting is the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: If lighting is the מצוה, 'put out and relight' makes sense. If placing were the מצוה, the ברייתא should have said to lift the lantern and set it down again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say lighting is the מצוה, that works well. But if placing is the מצוה, then instead of 'put it out and light it,' it should have said 'put it out, lift it, set it down, and light it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the lantern ברייתא proves its point. It tests the wording against each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If placing were the מצוה, the key act would be putting the lamp down. Then the ברייתא would need to mention lifting and setting it down again. It only mentions relighting, so the key act must be the lighting.

keyTerms.meaning: The lighting is what fulfills the מצוה
The placing is what fulfills the מצוה
It makes sense (according to one view)

steps.confusionAlert: Even the 'placing' view agrees the candle must be burning. The question is only which act counts as doing the מצוה: kindling the flame, or setting the lit lamp in its proper place.

phrases.english: It is understandable if you say
that lighting accomplishes the מצוה. Then it works well.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ הַנָּחָה עוֹשָׂה מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: But if you say that placing accomplishes the מצוה,
then this phrase, 'one extinguishes it and lights it,'

phrases.aramaic: מְכַבָּהּ וּמַגְבִּיהָהּ וּמַנִּיחָהּ וּמַדְלִיקָהּ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: should have said 'one extinguishes it, lifts it, sets it down, and lights it'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא הַדְלָקָה עוֹשָׂה מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 1.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא says only 'extinguish and relight' and leaves out lifting and placing.

steps.title: A second proof from the wording of the blessing
steps.stepSummary: The ברכה says 'to light the נר חנוכה,' so lighting must be the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also: since we say the ברכה 'who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us to light the נר חנוכה,' learn from this that lighting is the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second proof, this time from the words of the ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברכה names the act that fulfills the מצוה. The ברכה says 'to light' and not 'to place,' so lighting is the act that counts.

phrases.english: Furthermore: since we recite the blessing
'Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us'
'to light the Chanukah light'
learn from this that lighting accomplishes the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate proof to the one from the lantern.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the ברכה over נר חנוכה

steps.title: Conclusion: lighting is the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the proofs and closes the question: הדלקה עושה מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this conclusion, the long discussion of lighting versus placing is settled. The next steps build on this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling is הדלקה עושה מצוה. The act of lighting fulfills the מצוה of נר חנוכה, not the act of placing it.

phrases.english: Conclude from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proofs from steps 2 and 3.

steps.title: A חרש, שוטה, or קטן cannot light
steps.stepSummary: Since lighting is the מצוה, lighting done by a חרש, שוטה, or קטן is worth nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that we say lighting is the מצוה: if a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן lit it, he did nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a practical result from the conclusion it just reached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people are not obligated in מצוות, so their act cannot fulfill a מצוה. Because the lighting is the מצוה, their lighting does not count. An adult cannot fix it by picking up the lamp and placing it, since placing is not the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: And now that we say (introduces a result of the conclusion)
A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
He has done nothing at all

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical difference between the two views. Under the 'placing' view, an adult could place a lamp a קטן had lit and fulfill the מצוה.

phrases.english: And now that we say that lighting accomplishes the מצוה,
if a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor lit it,
he did nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion of step 4 in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lighting done by a חרש, שוטה, or קטן does not fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: A woman may certainly light
steps.stepSummary: A woman can light because, as רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches, women are obligated in נר חנוכה, since they too were part of the miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman certainly may light, as רבי יהושע בן לוי said: women are obligated in נר חנוכה, because they too were part of that miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא contrasts a woman with the people just listed. She is obligated, so her lighting counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test for lighting is whether the person is obligated. Women are obligated because they were also saved in the miracle. That is why a woman's lighting fulfills the מצוה even for others.

keyTerms.meaning: Because they too were part of that miracle

steps.confusionAlert: Women are generally exempt from מצוות that depend on a set time. Here they are still obligated, because of the special reason 'they too were part of the miracle.'

phrases.english: A woman certainly may light,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Women are obligated in the Chanukah light
because they too were included in that miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the other side of step 5: who does qualify to light.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may light, because women are obligated in נר חנוכה.

steps.title: A guest is obligated in נר חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that an אכסנאי (a guest staying away from home) is obligated in נר חנוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: a guest is obligated in נר חנוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: the duty of someone staying in another person's home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being away from home does not cancel the obligation. The guest must find a way to take part in a light, either by lighting himself or by joining the host's lighting.

keyTerms.meaning: A guest or lodger staying away from home

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
A guest is obligated in the Chanukah light.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אַכְסְנַאי חַיָּיב בְּנֵר חֲנוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a guest's obligation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אכסנאי is obligated in נר חנוכה.

steps.title: רבי זירא's practice as a guest
steps.stepSummary: As a single student, רבי זירא paid coins to become a partner in his host's light. After he married, he relied on his wife lighting for him at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: at first, when I was in the ישיבה, I would join in with coins together with my host. After I married, I said: now I surely don't need to, since they light for me in my house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing how רב ששת's rule works in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A guest can meet his obligation by paying toward the host's oil, which makes him a partner in the light. A married man away from home is covered because his household lights for him. This fits step 6: a wife's lighting counts.
steps.whatToRemember: A guest can fulfill נר חנוכה by paying to join his host's light. If his family lights for him at home, he does not need to do this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
At first, when I was in the yeshiva,
I would participate with coins together with my host.
After I married a wife, I said:
Now I certainly do not need to,
since they light on my behalf in my house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מֵרֵישׁ כִּי הֲוֵינָא בֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows step 7's rule in practice and adds the case of a married man.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guest joins the host's light by paying a share. A married man is covered by his household's lighting.

steps.title: All oils are fine, olive oil is best
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that any oil may be used for נר חנוכה, but olive oil is the best choice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: all oils are fine for the lamp, and olive oil is the very best.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: which oils may be used for the Chanukah lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no restriction on the type of oil for נר חנוכה. Still, olive oil is the preferred way to do the מצוה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
All oils are suitable for the lamp,
and olive oil is the most select.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הַשְּׁמָנִים כּוּלָּן יָפִין לַנֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about which oils to use.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All oils are valid for נר חנוכה, and שמן זית is the best.

steps.title: רבה switched from sesame oil to olive oil
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports that רבה first preferred sesame oil because it lasts longer. After hearing רבי יהושע בן לוי, he preferred olive oil because its light is clearer.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: at first my master would look for sesame oil, saying its light lasts longer. Once he heard רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching, he looked for olive oil, saying its light is clearer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing a great sage changing his practice to follow רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two reasonable goals: a longer-lasting light (sesame) or a clearer light (olive). After hearing that olive oil is best, רבה gave clarity priority over length.

keyTerms.meaning: Sought out, went out of his way for

steps.whatToRemember: Any oil is valid for נר חנוכה, but olive oil is preferred because its light is clearer. Even רבה changed his practice to follow this.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה מְהַדַּר מָר אַמִּשְׁחָא דְשׁוּמְשְׁמֵי.
phrases.english: At first, my Master (Rabba) would seek out sesame oil.
He said: Its light lasts longer.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דִּשְׁמַע לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: Once he heard this teaching of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
he sought out olive oil.
He said: Its light is clearer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה מְהַדַּר מָר אַמִּשְׁחָא דְשׁוּמְשְׁמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling from step 9 being put into practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Olive oil is preferred because its light is clearer, even though sesame oil lasts longer.

steps.title: All oils work for ink, olive oil is best
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that every oil can be used to make ink, but olive oil is the top choice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: All oils are good for ink, and olive oil is the very best.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from רבי יהושע בן לוי that sounds just like his נר חנוכה teaching in Step 9, but this one is about making ink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is quoted here because it has the same wording as Step 9: 'all oils are fine, olive oil is best.' This time the subject is ink, which was made from soot mixed with oil. It does not yet say how the olive oil is used, and the next step asks exactly that.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
All oils are good for ink,
and olive oil is the choicest.
phrases.notes: These are the same words he used in his teaching about the נר חנוכה back in Step 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching that is linked to Step 9 by its matching wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any oil may be used for ink; olive oil is best.

steps.title: Is olive oil best for mixing or for burning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what way olive oil is 'best' for ink: as the oil you knead into the soot, or as the oil you burn to make the soot.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Did he mean best for kneading, or best for making smoke?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the teaching it just quoted. It is setting up the next step, which will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ink was made in two stages. First you burn something to collect soot, and then you knead the soot together with oil. The question is which of these two stages רבי יהושע בן לוי was talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (a real unknown)
To knead or mix (oil into the soot)
To burn for smoke or soot

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
For kneading, or for smoking?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact meaning of Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether olive oil is best as the kneading oil or as the fuel for the soot.

steps.title: A ברייתא says olive oil is best both ways
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר זוטרא's ברייתא states that olive oil is best for both kneading and smoking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רב שמואל בר זוטרא taught: All oils are good for ink, and olive oil is the choicest, both for kneading and for smoking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a taught source that says 'both.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats the same words as רבי יהושע בן לוי and adds 'בין לגבל בין לעשן'. So you do not have to choose between the two meanings, because olive oil is best for both stages.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר זוּטְרָא:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Shmuel bar Zutra taught:
All oils are good for ink,
and olive oil is the choicest —
both for kneading and for smoking.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר זוּטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Olive oil is best for both kneading and smoking.

steps.title: Another version: all smoke works, olive oil is best
steps.stepSummary: A different version of רב שמואל בר זוטרא's teaching talks about kinds of smoke instead of kinds of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר זוטרא taught it this way: All kinds of smoke are good for ink, and olive oil is the choicest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of how רב שמואל בר זוטרא worded his teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the word 'oils' becomes 'smokes.' That means the teaching is only about the burning stage, and olive oil is the best fuel for making soot.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught it this way (a different version)

phrases.aramaic: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר זוּטְרָא מַתְנֵי הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Zutra taught it this way:
All kinds of smoke are good for ink,
and olive oil is the choicest.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר זוּטְרָא מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the source quoted in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any soot source is fine for ink; olive oil smoke is best.

steps.title: All saps work for ink, balsam sap is best
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches that every tree sap can be added to ink, and balsam sap is the best.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: All saps are good for ink, and balsam sap is better than all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more teaching built on the same pattern, this time about the sap that is mixed into ink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sap was added to make the ink stick and hold together. The pattern is the same as before: many things are allowed, and one is the best. This ends the side topic of ink.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
All saps are good for ink,
and balsam sap is better than all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching that closes the ink side topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any sap may be used in ink; balsam sap is best.

steps.title: The one who lights makes a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person who lights נר חנוכה must make a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: One who lights a נר חנוכה must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to נר חנוכה and starts a new topic: the ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the basic rule that lighting needs a ברכה, even though נר חנוכה is a rabbinic מצוה. The question of how a ברכה fits a rabbinic מצוה comes up later in Step 25.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
One who lights a Hanukkah light
must make a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the נר חנוכה discussion after the ink side topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lighting נר חנוכה requires a ברכה.

steps.title: Even the one who sees the lights makes a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה adds that someone who only sees the נרות חנוכה also makes a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ירמיה said: One who sees a נר חנוכה must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching extends the ברכה to a person who did not light but sees the lights burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of נר חנוכה is to publicize the miracle, so seeing the lights is also important. This is meant for someone who has not lit and has no one lighting for them.

phrases.english: And Rav Yirmeya said:
One who sees a Hanukkah light
must make a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to Step 16's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing נר חנוכה also requires a ברכה.

steps.title: How many ברכות on the first night and after
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה counts the ברכות. On night one the seer says 2 and the lighter says 3. After that the lighter says 2 and the seer says 1.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: On the first day, the one who sees makes two blessings and the one who lights makes three. From then on, the one who lights makes two and the one who sees makes one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the exact number of ברכות for each person on each night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lighter's three are להדליק, שעשה נסים, and שהחיינו. The seer does not say להדליק, since he is not lighting. After the first night one ברכה drops out for both of them, and the next steps ask which one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the ברכות we say on חנוכה today.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
On the first day, the one who sees makes two blessings,
and the one who lights makes three.
From then on, the one who lights makes two,
and the one who sees makes one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives details for the rules of Steps 16 and 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Night 1: lighter 3, seer 2. Later nights: lighter 2, seer 1.

steps.title: Which ברכה drops out after the first night?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ברכה is left out from the second night on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one does he leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רב יהודה's count. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the lighter and the seer lose one ברכה after night one, so we need to know which one it is.

phrases.english: What does he leave out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail of Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ברכה is dropped after the first night.

steps.title: שהחיינו drops out
steps.stepSummary: The ברכה of זמן (שהחיינו) is the one left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He leaves out the blessing of time (שהחיינו).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שהחיינו is the ברכה that drops out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שהחיינו thanks ה' for reaching a new season or time, so it is said only the first time each year.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה of שהחיינו (thanks for reaching this time)

phrases.english: He leaves out the blessing of time:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שהחיינו is dropped after the first night.

steps.title: Why not drop the miracle ברכה instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: perhaps שעשה נסים should be the one left out instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him leave out the blessing of the miracle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer and suggests a different ברכה could be dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle happened only once, so you might think thanking ה' for it once is enough. Then שעשה נסים could also be a first-night-only ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה of שעשה נסים (the miracle)

phrases.english: Let him leave out the miracle blessing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that זמן, and not נס, is the ברכה dropped.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The miracle happened once, so its ברכה could also be said once.

steps.title: The miracle lasted every day
steps.stepSummary: The miracle was present on all eight days, so its ברכה is said every night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The miracle was there on all the days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the miracle belongs to each day, so its ברכה cannot be dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil kept burning every one of the eight days, which makes each day its own miracle. שהחיינו is about the season arriving, and that only happens once.

keyTerms.meaning: It is present on all the days

steps.whatToRemember: After night one, the lighter says להדליק and שעשה נסים, and the seer says only שעשה נסים. שהחיינו is said on the first night only.

phrases.english: The miracle exists on all the days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction about how long each ברכה's reason lasts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The miracle ברכה is needed only once.
steps.terutzMaskana: The miracle was present every day, so its ברכה is said nightly; זמן applies only once.

steps.title: What is the wording of the ברכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the lighting ברכה actually says.
steps.simpleTranslation: What blessing does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the wording of the main ברכה. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exact wording matters because the next question depends on it.

phrases.english: What blessing does he say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the ברכה from Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the lighting ברכה.

steps.title: 'אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו להדליק'
steps.stepSummary: The ברכה is: 'Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us to light the נר של חנוכה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He says: 'Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us to light the נר של חנוכה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the wording of the ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וצונו' (He commanded us) says that ה' gave this מצוה. That leads to an obvious problem, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Who made us holy with His commandments

phrases.english: He says:
"Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us to light the Hanukkah light."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording: אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו להדליק נר של חנוכה.

steps.title: Where did ה' command us about חנוכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can say 'וצונו' when חנוכה is not in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where did He command us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of 'He commanded us,' since נר חנוכה is a rabbinic מצוה. The answers come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנוכה happened long after the תורה was given. So the question is how a מצוה made by the חכמים can be called a command from ה'.

keyTerms.meaning: And where did He command us?

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not challenging the מצוה itself. It only asks how the word 'וצונו' fits a מצוה that comes from the חכמים.

phrases.english: And where did He command us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording given in Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The תורה basis for calling a rabbinic מצוה a command of ה'.

steps.title: Source: 'לא תסור'
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא says the source is the פסוק 'לא תסור', which commands us to obey the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא said: From 'You shall not turn aside.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא gives a פסוק that makes obeying the חכמים a תורה command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים י״ז tells us not to turn away from what the חכמים rule. So when we follow their מצוה, we are also fulfilling ה''s command, and that is why we can say 'וצונו'.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not turn aside (from the words of the חכמים)

phrases.english: Rav Avya said:
From "You shall not turn aside."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The command comes from לא תסור (Deuteronomy 17:11).

steps.title: Source: 'שאל אביך ויגדך'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמיה gives a different פסוק: 'Ask your father and he will tell you, your elders and they will say to you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמיה said: 'Ask your father and he will tell you, your elders and they will say to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers another פסוק for the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers agree that we must listen to the חכמים. They differ only about which פסוק teaches it. רב נחמיה uses a פסוק from דברים ל״ב about learning from the elders.

keyTerms.meaning: Ask your father and he will tell you

phrases.english: Rav Nechemya said:
"Ask your father and he will tell you,
your elders and they will say to you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another source in place of Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The command comes from שאל אביך ויגדך (Deuteronomy 32:7).

steps.title: דמאי: a rabbinic rule with no ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם quotes a משנה that lets you separate tithes from דמאי while undressed. That shows no ברכה is said, which seems to contradict the idea that every rabbinic מצוה needs a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם objected: With דמאי, one may use it for an עירוב and a שיתוף, make a blessing over it, make a זימון over it, and separate its tithes while undressed and at dusk. Now if you say every rabbinic rule needs a blessing, how can he bless while standing undressed? We need 'your camp shall be holy', and that is missing!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם challenges the idea from Steps 24-27 that every rabbinic מצוה gets a ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating tithes from דמאי is a rabbinic rule, yet the משנה lets you do it undressed. A person who is undressed may not say a ברכה, because of the פסוק 'והיה מחניך קדוש'. So it looks like this rabbinic מצוה has no ברכה, which goes against the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed
Your camp shall be holy (no ברכה when undressed)

phrases.english: Rav Amram objected:
Demai: one may make an eiruv with it,
and make a shituf with it,
and make a blessing over it and make a zimun over it,
and separate its tithes undressed and at twilight.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ כׇּל מִדְּרַבָּנַן בָּעֵי בְּרָכָה,
phrases.english: And if you say every rabbinic rule needs a blessing,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא כִּי קָאֵי עָרוֹם הֵיכִי מְבָרֵךְ?
phrases.english: here, when he stands undressed, how can he bless?
But we need "your camp shall be holy" —
and it is missing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the general rule that came out of Steps 24-27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that every rabbinic מצוה requires a ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tithing דמאי is rabbinic, yet it may be done undressed, where no ברכה is possible. So rabbinic מצוות do not always get a ברכה.

steps.title: A definite rabbinic מצוה gets a ברכה; a rule made for a doubt does not
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a definite rabbinic מצוה needs a ברכה, but a rabbinic rule made because of a doubt, like דמאי, does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A definite rabbinic rule needs a blessing; a rabbinic rule made because of a doubt does not need a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב עמרם by dividing rabbinic rules into two kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נר חנוכה is a definite rabbinic מצוה, so it has a ברכה. דמאי is a rule made only because the produce might not have been tithed, which is a doubt, so it has no ברכה. That is why tithing דמאי while undressed is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic rule made because of a doubt

steps.whatToRemember: A definite rabbinic מצוה, like נר חנוכה, gets a ברכה with 'וצונו'. A rule made because of a doubt, like דמאי, gets no ברכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction is a basic rule of when we make ברכות on rabbinic מצוות.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A definite rabbinic rule needs a blessing,
a rabbinic rule because of a doubt does not need a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between categories (definite vs. doubt-based rabbinic rules)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every rabbinic rule needs a ברכה, so דמאי should too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only definite rabbinic מצוות need a ברכה; rules made because of a doubt, like דמאי, do not.

steps.title: יום טוב שני is based on doubt, yet it needs a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: יום טוב שני is a rabbinic rule made because of a doubt, and we still say ברכות on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't יום טוב שני a rabbinic rule made because of a doubt? And it still needs a ברכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's rule from Step 29. אביי said rabbinic rules made because of a doubt do not need a ברכה, but יום טוב שני does need one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום טוב שני was set up because people outside ארץ ישראל long ago were unsure which day was the real יום טוב. That makes it a 'doubt rule', just like דמאי. Yet we say קידוש, תפילה, and other ברכות on it, so אביי's rule seems to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The second day of a festival kept outside ארץ ישראל
A rabbinic rule made because of a doubt
'But isn't it…?', which opens a challenge

phrases.english: But isn't the second day of Yom Tov
a rabbinic rule made because of doubt,
and it requires a blessing?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי דִּסְפֵק דִּבְרֵיהֶם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's distinction from Step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that a rabbinic rule based on doubt needs no ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יום טוב שני is a rabbinic rule based on doubt, yet it needs a ברכה, which is a counterexample

steps.title: The second day gets a blessing so people won't take it lightly
steps.stepSummary: יום טוב שני is a special exception: the חכמים required ברכות so that people would not treat the day lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is so that people will not treat it with disrespect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי. יום טוב שני is an exception, and it gets ברכות for a special reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's general rule still stands: doubt-based rules normally get no ברכה. יום טוב שני is still a doubt-based rule, but the חכמים made a special exception for it. Without ברכות, people might treat it as a weekday and break its holiness.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think יום טוב שני stops being a 'doubt rule'. It still is one. It is just an exception, and it gets a ברכה for a different reason.

phrases.english: There
it is so that they will not treat it lightly.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לִיזַלְזְלוּ בֵּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a special reason applies to יום טוב שני
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יום טוב שני is a doubt rule that gets a ברכה, so אביי's rule is wrong
steps.terutzMaskana: יום טוב שני is an exception made to protect its honor. The general rule stands.

steps.title: רבא: most עמי הארץ do tithe, so דמאי is not a real doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different explanation. דמאי gets no ברכה because most עמי הארץ really do tithe, so it is only a weak worry and not a true doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Most unlearned people do separate tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers another way to explain why דמאי needs no ברכה. This avoids אביי's distinction, and with it the challenge from יום טוב שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, דמאי is not a real doubt at all. Most עמי הארץ tithe, so tithing דמאי is just extra caution, and no ברכה was set up for it. A rule based on a true doubt, like יום טוב שני, does get a ברכה like any other rabbinic מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Unlearned people who were not careful about all מצוות

steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches. אביי says doubt-based rabbinic rules get no ברכה, and יום טוב שני is an exception. רבא says דמאי is not a real doubt because most people tithe. That is why דמאי gets no ברכה, while real doubt-based rules do.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Most unlearned people
do separate tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: רוֹב עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מְעַשְּׂרִין הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to רב עמרם's קשיא (Step 28), instead of אביי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: דמאי is not a true doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tithing דמאי is a rabbinic מצוה, so by the rule 'every rabbinic מצוה needs a ברכה' it should need one, and it could not be done undressed.
steps.terutzMaskana: דמאי is only extra caution, since most people tithe. That is why it gets no ברכה.

steps.title: A חצר with two entrances needs two נרות חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a חצר with two openings needs a נר חנוכה at each opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: A courtyard that has two entrances needs two lights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about lighting נר חנוכה. רב הונא says each of the two entrances of a חצר needs its own light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back then, people lit at the entrance of the courtyard facing the street. If one entrance has no light, people might think the owner did not light at all. The reason is not stated yet; the גמרא works it out in Steps 35-37.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
A courtyard that has two entrances
requires two lights.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: חָצֵר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי פְּתָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about where to place נר חנוכה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two entrances to a חצר each need a נר חנוכה

steps.title: רבא: only when the entrances face different directions
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits רב הונא's rule. Two lights are needed only when the entrances are on two different sides. If both are on the same side, one light is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We only said this when the entrances are on two sides. But if they are on one side, a second light is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows רב הונא's rule to entrances that face different directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both openings face the same street, anyone passing sees both, so they will see the one light. If the openings face different streets, a person who passes the dark one cannot tell that the house lit at the other.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this in the case of… (a limiting phrase)

phrases.english: Rava said:
We only said this for two directions,
but for one direction, it is not needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב הונא's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two lights are needed only when the entrances face two different directions

steps.title: What is the reason, and whose suspicion are we worried about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבא's rule. If the reason is suspicion, whose suspicion does it mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you say it is because of suspicion, whose suspicion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא divides the cases this way. It suggests 'suspicion' and asks who would be suspicious. This sets up a two-sided problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that people will see a dark entrance and suspect the owner did not light. The גמרא needs to know which group of people it means, because each answer leads to a different result.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say… (suggesting a possible answer)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If you say it is because of suspicion,
whose suspicion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבא's limitation
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for רבא's distinction, and which people's suspicion it refers to

steps.title: Neither outsiders nor locals fit רבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: Outsiders would suspect even when both entrances are on one side. Locals would not suspect even when the entrances are on two sides. Neither choice fits רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the suspicion of people in general, then even with entrances on one side a second light should be needed! If it is the suspicion of the local people, then even with entrances on two sides it should not be needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that both possible answers clash with רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outsiders do not know the two openings belong to one house, so they would suspect in every case, even with one direction. Locals know the house has two openings and would assume he lit at the other one, so they would never suspect. Either way, the line רבא drew does not seem to make sense.

phrases.english: If you say it is the suspicion of people in general,
then even for one direction it should also be required!
If it is the suspicion of the town's residents,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ מִשְׁתֵּי רוּחוֹת נָמֵי לָא לִיבְעֵי.
phrases.english: then even for two directions it should not be required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a two-sided problem from the question in Step 35
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's distinction between one direction and two directions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Outsiders' suspicion would require two lights in every case. Locals' suspicion would never require them. Neither fits רבא's middle position.

steps.title: It is the locals' suspicion, because they may pass only one entrance
steps.stepSummary: The suspicion is from the local people. A local may pass only the dark entrance and wrongly assume the owner did not light at the other one either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is because of the suspicion of the local people. Sometimes they pass by this entrance and not by that one, and they say: 'Just as he did not light at this entrance, he did not light at that entrance either.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that it means the locals' suspicion. It explains why locals can still be suspicious when the entrances face different directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Locals know both openings belong to one house. But if the openings face different streets, a local may walk past only the dark one and conclude the other is dark too. With both openings on one side, he sees both at once, so there is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (keeps one side of the choice)

steps.whatToRemember: Two openings facing different sides need two lights. The worry is that locals who pass only one side will think the owner did not light.

phrases.english: Really, it is because of the suspicion of the town's residents,
and sometimes they pass by this one
and do not pass by that one,
and they say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דִּבְהַאי פִּיתְחָא לָא אַדְלִיק —
phrases.english: Just as at this entrance he did not light,
at that entrance he also did not light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the dilemma of Step 36
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing one side of the dilemma and refining it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Locals would never suspect, since they know the house has two openings
steps.terutzMaskana: Locals who pass only one opening may assume both are dark, so two lights are needed when the openings face different sides

steps.title: Where do we learn that we worry about suspicion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that הלכה takes חשד into account.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that we are concerned about suspicion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the idea that worrying about what people might suspect is a real halachic concern. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 37 built the rule on חשד. Now the גמרא wants to show that this kind of concern is grounded in earlier sources, so that it is not just a new idea.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this?
We are concerned / we take into account

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that we are concerned about suspicion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the principle used in Step 37
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that halacha worries about suspicion

steps.title: רבי שמעון: four reasons to leave פאה at the end of the field
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון: the תורה says to leave פאה at the end of the field for four reasons, and one of them is חשד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי שמעון said: For four reasons the תורה said to leave פאה at the end of one's field: because of stealing from the poor, because of wasting the poor people's time, because of suspicion, and because of 'do not finish off completely'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. One of the reasons for the law of פאה is 'suspicion', which proves the תורה itself cares about suspicion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving פאה at the very end of the field, and not in the middle, is partly explained by מפני החשד. Since the תורה shapes a law to avoid suspicion, the חכמים can do the same for נר חנוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor
'Do not finish off completely' (the פסוק's wording)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that חשד, the worry about how things look to others, is a concern the תורה itself takes into account. It is not only an extra stringency.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon said:
Because of four things
the Torah said to leave pe'ah
at the end of his field:
because of stealing from the poor,
and because of wasting the poor people's time,
and because of suspicion,
and because of 'do not finish off completely.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: בִּשְׁבִיל אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 38 with a source
steps.raayaObject: The principle that we are concerned about חשד
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי שמעון about leaving פאה at the end of the field

steps.title: Explaining the first reason: stealing from the poor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains 'stealing from the poor'. If פאה could be left anywhere, the owner might wait for a moment with no poor people around and give it to a poor relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Because of stealing from the poor': so that the owner will not watch for a moment when no one is around and say to his poor relative, 'This is פאה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts explaining its four reasons one by one, beginning with the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If פאה could be set aside in the middle of harvesting, the owner could pick a quiet moment and hand it to a relative. The other poor people would lose their share. Fixing פאה at the end of the field keeps it open to everyone. The explanation of 'suspicion', which is the reason the גמרא needs, comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A free moment, when no one is around

phrases.english: Because of stealing from the poor:
so that the owner will not see
a free moment
and say to his poor relative:
'This is pe'ah.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי גֶּזֶל עֲנִיִּים — שֶׁלֹּא יִרְאֶה בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the four reasons listed in Step 39
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פאה goes at the end of the field so the owner cannot secretly give it to a poor relative and rob the other poor people
